Everything on this page is optional and off by default. The extension can also dress up the site *around* your charts: self-hosted fonts, a Quarto theme in the same colors as the panels, and a few pieces of site chrome (a collapsible sidebar, a sidebar search box, a category cloud above a listing, embedding, a Share button, a "Report bug" popup). Each is one key under `mathviz:` in `_quarto.yml`, or under `mathviz-page:` in one page's front matter for a piece only that page uses (never `mathviz:` there -- see [Options for one page](install.qmd#page-options)). A site pays only for the pieces it turns on.

These come with the Quarto extension only. The plain script bundle doesn't include them.

## All the keys

```yaml
mathviz:
  fonts: true
  sidebar-rail: my-site-sidebar-pinned     # or true
  sidebar-search: true
  category-cloud: true
  embed: true
  share:
    site-url: https://example.com
    embed-docs: embed.html
  report-bug:
    repo: owner/name
    branch: main
```

| Key | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `fonts` | `true` | Serves Inter and JetBrains Mono from your own site. |
| `sidebar-rail` | `true`, or a storage key | Hides Quarto's sidebar behind a slim rail at the left edge. |
| `sidebar-search` | `true` | Adds a search box at the top of the sidebar that narrows it to matching titles. |
| `category-cloud` | `true` | Moves a listing's category cloud above its cards and adds an "All" entry. |
| `embed` | `true` | Lets another site show one app alone in an `<iframe>`. |
| `share` | a map (see [Share](#share)) | Adds a "Share" button to every app. Turns `embed` on too. |
| `report-bug` | a map with `repo` (required) and `branch` | Adds a "Report bug" popup when a reader selects text. |

Where a key takes a **storage key**, the string names the `localStorage` entry that remembers the reader's choice. Name your own if two sites share one origin (two GitHub Pages project sites, say), or if your privacy page lists what you store. With `true` the default is `vm-sidebar-pinned`.

## Fonts

```yaml
mathviz:
  fonts: true
```

Serves Inter (text) and JetBrains Mono (code) from your own `site_libs/`, so no page makes a request to Google Fonts. Browsers download only the character sets a page uses; an English page costs about 105 kB. It's off by default because a site with its own typography doesn't need the files.

Turning `fonts` on only makes the fonts available. The [theme](#theme) is what uses them. With your own theme, name `"Inter"` or `"JetBrains Mono"` in your own CSS.

## Theme {#theme}

The Quarto theme gives Bootstrap's navbar, links, cards, callouts, tables, blockquotes, category chips, listing controls and footer the same colors as the mathviz panels, in light and dark. In dark mode it also puts a light backing behind SVG, PNG and GIF figures, which are usually drawn for a white page. List it **before** your own theme file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: [_extensions/apurvanakade/mathviz/theme/mathviz-light.scss, custom-light.scss]
      dark:  [_extensions/apurvanakade/mathviz/theme/mathviz-dark.scss, custom-dark.scss]
```

To change a color, set the matching `$vm-*` variable in your own file's `/*-- scss:defaults --*/` section. `$vm-accent`, for example, changes the link color and the panels' `--vm-accent` together:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$vm-accent: #b5179e;
```

The variables are `$vm-bg`, `$vm-surface`, `$vm-surface-hover`, `$vm-text`, `$vm-text-soft`, `$vm-border`, `$vm-accent`, `$vm-accent-hover`, `$vm-on-accent`, `$vm-grid`, `$vm-radius`, `$vm-radius-sm`, `$vm-shadow` and `$vm-shadow-color`. Their defaults are the [tokens](theming.qmd#the-tokens) of the same name. Five more set the type: `$vm-font-size-root` (the size every rem scales from, default 17px), `$vm-font-weight-display` (page titles, 300), `$vm-font-weight-heading` (section headings, 500), `$vm-h2-font-size` (1.35rem) and `$vm-h3-font-size` (1.1rem). The theme sets the fonts to Inter and JetBrains Mono, falling back to system fonts; add `fonts: true` to make sure readers actually get them.

### Listing cards {#cards}

A grid listing's cards have no border or background: each is its image, rounded, with the title and description under it. On hover a card rises slightly and a soft panel appears around it, and the title turns the accent color. The panel reaches `$vm-card-lift-pad` (default `0.75rem`) past the card on every side, so leave at least that much room around a grid.

Cards are at most `$vm-card-width` wide (default `18rem`, about 300px), so the number of cards in a row follows the page's width; a listing's `grid-columns` no longer sets it. On a phone one card fills the column. Each listing's own `image-height` still sets its images' height.

## Tagging an app: `vm-app` {#vm-app}

Embedding and Share both work on an **app**: the block holding a page's controls and chart. Mark it with the `vm-app` class:

```markdown
::: {.vm-app}
<!-- the ojs-panel, the ojs-chart-block, ... -->
:::
```

If a page has more than one app, give each an id: `::: {.vm-app #doors}`.

## Embedding

```yaml
mathviz:
  embed: true
```

Adding `?embed=1` to a page's URL shows only the page's first app: no navbar, sidebar, title, footer or comments. `?embed=<id>` shows the app with that id instead, and `?embed=<n>` the n-th app on the page (what the Share dialog uses for an app without an id). Another site then frames it:

```html
<iframe
  src="https://example.com/apps/newton/?embed=1"
  width="100%" height="900" loading="lazy"
  title="Newton's method">
</iframe>
```

A page's own URL parameters (the inputs it syncs into the URL) still work, so a frame can open at particular inputs. Inside a frame, the sidebar rail, Share button and Report bug popup stay hidden.

## Share {#share}

```yaml
mathviz:
  share:
    site-url: https://example.com
    embed-docs: embed.html
```

Puts a "Share" button above every `vm-app`. It opens a dialog with the page's link, with and without the current inputs, and a ready-to-paste `<iframe>` snippet.

- `site-url` is your site's public address. Set it: the links then work even when copied from `quarto preview` or a test deploy. (Quarto doesn't pass `website.site-url` to extensions, so you write it again here.)
- `embed-docs` is optional: a page on your site, relative to its root, that the dialog links to as "Embedding an app".

## Category cloud {#category-cloud}

```yaml
mathviz:
  category-cloud: true
```

Usually only one page has a cloud, so you can turn it on there alone, in that page's front matter:

```yaml
mathviz-page:
  category-cloud: true
```

For a listing with `categories: cloud`. Quarto puts the cloud in the right margin, which is narrow beside a grid and hidden on a phone. This moves it above the listing's cards and adds an "All" entry first, which clears the filter. Clicking a category works as before, every entry can also be reached with Tab and picked with Enter or Space, and the page's `#category=` links still open it filtered. Back and Forward step through the categories picked, "All" included. When a pick leaves the cloud above the window (a tag clicked on a card far down shortens the page), the page scrolls back to it; give `.vm-category-cloud` a `scroll-margin-top` if a fixed navbar would cover it. The page then has no margin column, so the listing gets the width. Without JavaScript the cloud stays in the margin.

The cloud is unstyled: it looks the way Quarto draws it until your own CSS restyles it. Style it with these classes:

| Selector | Is |
|---|---|
| `.vm-category-cloud` | the wrapper around the moved cloud |
| `.vm-category-cloud .category` | each entry, "All" included |
| `.vm-category-cloud .category--all` | the "All" entry |
| `.vm-category-cloud .category.active` | the selected entry; "All" while nothing is filtered |

```css
.vm-category-cloud .quarto-listing-category { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.3rem 0.6rem; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
.vm-category-cloud .category { cursor: pointer; color: var(--vm-text-soft); }
.vm-category-cloud .category.active { color: var(--vm-accent); font-weight: 500; }
```

With more than one listing on the page, the cloud goes above the first grid, default or table listing (not a custom-template one), and filters all of them, as Quarto's does.

## Sidebar rail {#sidebar-rail}

```yaml
mathviz:
  sidebar-rail: true
```

For a site with Quarto sidebar navigation (`style: floating` or `docked`). The sidebar is hidden at every width, behind a slim rail at the left edge with two buttons: one to open it, one to pin it open (remembered across pages). Escape or a click outside closes it. The body column takes the sidebar's space and is as wide as your `grid: body-width` (Quarto's 800px if unset); a page with a table of contents keeps its right margin.

It changes nothing on a site or page that doesn't turn it on, or on a page without a sidebar: to switch it off for one page, set `mathviz-page: {sidebar-rail: false}`.


```yaml
mathviz:
  sidebar-search: true
```

For a site with Quarto sidebar navigation, with or without the rail. A search box at the top of the sidebar narrows the menu as the reader types. It searches titles only, not page text: Quarto's own full-text search allows one box per page, so keep that one in the navbar.

- Each word typed must start a word of a title, in any order: "ode" finds "Methods for ODEs" but not "Model Fitting". Case, accents and punctuation are ignored, and so are apostrophes, straight or curly.
- A section whose own title matches keeps everything under it. Any other section shows only its matching entries and disappears when it has none. Sections open while a search is active and go back to how they were when it is cleared.
- Enter opens the first matching page. Escape clears the box and goes no further, so a second Escape closes the rail (or reaches a handler of the site's own).
- Nothing is stored.

## Report bug

```yaml
mathviz:
  report-bug:
    repo: owner/name
    branch: main      # the default
```

When a reader selects text, a small "Report bug" button appears next to it. Clicking it opens a new GitHub issue in `repo`, labelled `bug`, with the page's URL, a link to the page's `.qmd` source on `branch`, and the selected text quoted. The source link assumes the Quarto project is at the repository root. Without `repo` the key is skipped with a warning.
